issues.t: Valve springs can break and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, misfires, unusual engine noise, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: Some valve springs on early cars (sold as the 2013 Scion FR-S) were weak and could fracture.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces the valve springs for free; the engine has to come out, so allow time.

issues.t: Engine knock or failure after the valve spring recall repair
issues.sym: Knocking or rod-like noise, low oil pressure light, loss of power or sudden engine shutdown, often within days to a few thousand miles of the valve spring recall work.
issues.why: Many owners report bearing damage after the recall repair. Excess sealant or debris reaching the oil pickup and starving the bearings of oil is the most common explanation given, though it has not been officially confirmed.
issues.next: If the recall was done and you hear knocking, stop driving and have the oil pan and pickup inspected. Keep the recall paperwork and ask Toyota for goodwill help.

issues.t: Engine knock or sudden engine failure
issues.sym: Knocking that gets louder, smoke, misfires or the engine dying, sometimes with no warning lights.
issues.why: Owners report bottom-end failures and broken valve parts outside of the recall. Low oil level and hard driving make it worse.
issues.next: Check the oil level often, since these engines can use some oil. If you hear knocking, stop driving and have it diagnosed before it seizes.

issues.t: Rough idle or stalling with cam timing codes
issues.sym: Idle speed that hunts up and down, shudder, stalling when you come to a stop, and a check engine light with codes P0016 to P0019.
issues.why: The variable valve timing controllers on early engines did not always meet tolerances. A faulty cam sprocket can also lose oil pressure so the cam timing cannot respond.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a dealer about the engine computer update. If it still stalls, the cam sprocket may need replacing.

issues.t: Clutch release bearing noise or failure
issues.sym: Chirping, squealing or screeching that changes when you press the clutch, gears that grind when shifting, or a clutch pedal that feels different.
issues.why: The clutch release (throw-out) bearing on manual cars can wear out early.
issues.next: Have the clutch inspected soon. Replacing the bearing with the clutch before it fails can prevent damage to the transmission.

issues.t: Fuel pump chirp, whine or failure
issues.sym: A chirp or whine from the fuel system, hard starting, sputtering when you accelerate, or the engine cutting out.
issues.why: The engine has both a high-pressure fuel pump and an in-tank pump. A chirping high-pressure pump can be an early sign of wear, and in-tank pumps have failed.
issues.next: If the car stalls or struggles to start, have fuel pressure tested. Check for open recalls on 2018 and 2019 models.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure causes misfires
issues.sym: Shaking or stumbling under power and a check engine light with a coil or misfire code.
issues.why: The coils on the passenger-side cylinders sit close to the hot exhaust header, and heat makes them fail sooner, especially on cars that see track use.
issues.next: Have the codes read and replace the failed coil. Heat shielding can help if the car is driven hard.

issues.t: Power steering binds, clunks or loses assist
issues.sym: The steering feels notchy or stiff, clunks or rattles, or suddenly gets heavy.
issues.why: Owners report failures in the electric power steering, including worn dampers or bushings and motor problems.
issues.next: Have the steering checked right away if it binds or loses assist. Report it to NHTSA if it happened while driving.

issues.t: Fuel pump clicks off early when filling up
issues.sym: The gas station pump keeps shutting off before the tank is full, or fuel spills out while filling, sometimes with an EVAP check engine code.
issues.why: A problem in the charcoal canister or vapor venting system stops the tank from venting properly during refueling.
issues.next: Have the EVAP system smoke-tested and the charcoal canister checked.

issues.t: Key can be removed when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: On automatics with a regular key, you can pull the key out without the shifter in Park, and the car could roll away.
issues.why: The key-to-shifter interlock was disabled for shipping and was not always reconnected.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer inspects and reconnects the interlock wiring for free.

issues.t: Spare tire may be underinflated (recall)
issues.sym: The temporary spare is low on air when you need it.
issues.why: Some spares left the factory without being filled to the pressure on the tire label.
issues.next: Check the spare's pressure yourself, and ask a dealer about the recall check.

issues.t: In-tank fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light, the car not starting, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank may fail.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces the pump for free.

issues.t: Engine failure from sealant clogging the oil pickup
issues.sym: Sudden knocking, an oil pressure light, power loss or the engine shutting down, sometimes at low mileage and with no warning.
issues.why: On some cars, too much silicone sealant was applied to the oil pan at the factory. Pieces break off and block the oil pickup screen, starving the bearings of oil.
issues.next: Ask a shop or dealer to drop the oil pan and clean the pickup, or at least look inside with a camera and cut open the old oil filter. If you hear knocking, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Oil pressure drops during hard cornering on track
issues.sym: On track or autocross, the oil pressure dips in long, fast corners. Some engines have spun a rod bearing.
issues.why: Independent testing found oil pressure falling sharply in sustained high-speed right-hand corners at high rpm, likely from oil moving away from the pickup.
issues.next: If you track the car, fit an oil pressure gauge, keep the oil at the full mark and talk to your dealer about warranty rules. Normal street driving is far less affected.

issues.t: Rear turn signals stop working in bright sun (recall)
issues.sym: In strong sunlight the rear turn signals stop flashing and the front ones flash fast.
issues.why: Strong sun on the rear lamp electronics makes the car think a bulb has failed and shut the rear signals off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer replaces both rear lamp assemblies for free.

issues.t: Remote start and app features stop working
issues.sym: Toyota app features such as remote start stop working, often about a year after the car was built.
issues.why: The car's built-in cellular module was not activated or was programmed in a way that cut off service.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to activate or reprogram the data communication module under the service bulletin.

issues.t: Fuel lines rub through their covers under the hood
issues.sym: Worn or flattened spots on the fuel lines on the right side of the engine bay near the intake, and possibly a fuel smell.
issues.why: Owners report the fuel lines rubbing against nearby parts or each other while the engine runs, which wears through the protective sleeve.
issues.next: Open the hood and look at the fuel lines near the intake. If they are worn, have a dealer reposition or replace them before they leak.

issues.t: Oil leak from spark plug tube seals
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the top of the cylinder heads, burning oil smell, or a misfire if oil reaches the plugs.
issues.why: The seals around the spark plug tubes can crack and let oil out.
issues.next: Have a shop find the leak and replace the cracked seals while under warranty.

issues.t: Load capacity label shows the wrong weight (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The door-jamb label may show the wrong added weight for dealer-installed accessories.
issues.why: On some cars with distributor-installed accessories, the load label had incorrect weight values, which could lead to overloading.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A corrected label is mailed for free.

issues.t: Blind spot alerts late or missing
issues.sym: The blind spot light comes on late or not at all when a car is beside you.
issues.why: An owner reported intermittent blind spot warnings; the dealer reproduced it but found no fault codes.
issues.next: Always check over your shoulder. Keep the rear bumper corners clean and have a dealer check the radar sensors.
